judged_text: The recurring-series deletion block (all user credentials x all updatedBookings) now sits inside the per-reference loop, so it executes once per calendar reference instead of once per cancellation, and it iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials. Cancelling a recurring collective booking with two calendar references issues every updated booking's deleteEvent twice — the second pass 404s into the swallowed inner catch — and events created with team members' credentials are never touched because only the organizer's credentials are enumerated, while the cancellation reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-series deletion logic (the `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` branch that builds `promises` over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and loops `for (const updBooking of updatedBookings)`) is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Since `bookingCalendarReference` is now an array (`filter`) and can contain multiple calendar references, this block will execute once per reference, re-enumerating the same `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and re-deleting the same `updatedBookings` events multiple times. Errors from the duplicated deletions are caught and only logged (`try { await Promise.all(promises); } catch { logger.error(...) }`), so the cancellation can proceed without surfacing failure. Also, the enumeration is limited to `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, so events created under other participants' credentials (e.g., collective/team members) are not targeted by this deletion pass.
